title: Playing with young bands; the Eureka band
summary: He played with unnamed neighborhood bands as a learner, and names the Eureka band as the oldest colored band in town.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: There was a regular band at that time. The team was in full blush, you know? And you took up the alto horn?
Oh, I wasn't playing in the band. No, no, but you started on the alto horn then. Yeah. I see you.
You say you started to play alto when you was 14, huh?
When did you play in the band?
How long it took you before you joined in the band? How old you was when you played in the band?
Well, I used to be in a band all the time. I used to go to different relations, you know? The parents would invite me. You see, I was anxious to learn. They'd invite me to come.
Was that a band, a brass band on the street or a dance band? Brass band. Brass band. Yeah. What band was it? Did it have a name and a leader?
Did a band have a name and who was the leader?
Take your time. Take your time. They had so many bands. I'm telling all the young fellas, you know? Yeah. Different names, you know?
They had Eureka band. You remember that? That was the main bands around the town, you know?
You say, what was the first band you played with when you first started to play music? Do you know the name of the first band you played with?
I used to play with bands that didn't have no name at all, you know? All the young fellas, you know?
Well, get one that had a name. The first one that had a name.
Get the first one you played with had a name. That's what they want.
That was the oldest band in town. I like that. Colored, you know? Eureka.
